statement_record.book: If A is a full subcategory of C and every object of C is isomorphic (in C) to some object of A, then the inclusion K : A -> C is an equivalence of categories and is part of an adjoint equivalence <T, K; eta, 1> : C -> A whose counit is the identity; therefore A is reflective in C. Special case: A a skeleton of C.
statement_record.intree: FF_ESO_Equivalence: any Full + Faithful + EssentiallySurjective functor is an EquivalenceOfCategories; Equivalence_to_AdjointEquivalence refines any equivalence into an AdjointEquivalence (unit and counit componentwise isomorphisms); Reflective packages full subcategory + reflector + reflector ⊣ Incl.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: the general FF+Faithful+ESO theorem subsumes the equivalence claim once instantiated at Incl (iso-density = EssentiallySurjective (Incl), fullness via Full_Implies_Full_Functor, faithfulness of Incl trivial but with no generic instance), yet no in-tree statement performs that specialization; the book's identity counit (strict <T, K; eta, 1>) is only an isomorphism in-tree; and the corollary 'A is reflective in C' is never derived from iso-density (Reflective exists but has no constructor from these hypotheses).

gap: No in-tree specialization of FF_ESO_Equivalence to the inclusion of a full isomorphism-dense subcategory (concrete instances of the pattern exist: Karoubi_Embed in Construction/Karoubi/Universal.v:502, idem_G in Construction/Reflective/Idempotent.v:465, RT_Comparison in Construction/Grothendieck/RoundTrip.v:1589, but no general subcategory statement); no generic Faithful (Incl C S) instance (asserted in comments, proven per-instance, e.g. Sheaves_Faithful); the identity-counit strictness of the book's adjoint equivalence is not representable in the delivered form (counit only a componentwise iso); reflectivity of the iso-dense full subcategory is not concluded.

statement_record.book: If S : A -> C is full, faithful, and surjective on objects (every c equals S a for some a), then there is an adjoint equivalence <T, S; 1, epsilon> : C -> A whose unit is the identity, and hence T is a left-adjoint-right-inverse of S.
statement_record.intree: FF_ESO_Equivalence + Equivalence_to_AdjointEquivalence: a full, faithful, essentially surjective functor is an equivalence, refinable to an AdjointEquivalence whose unit and counit are componentwise isomorphisms.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree hypotheses weaker (essential surjectivity, entailed by strict surjectivity with identity witnesses, so the in-tree theorem applies to the book's hypotheses); intree conclusion weaker: the unit is delivered only as a natural isomorphism, never as the identity transformation, and there is no left-adjoint-right-inverse packaging.

gap: The strict refinement is missing: no statement that under on-the-nose surjectivity on objects the quasi-inverse T can be chosen with S (T c) = c and identity unit (a strictness the setoid house style deliberately avoids, per the Theory/Equivalence.v essay), and no left-adjoint-right-inverse vocabulary (see the ABSENT record for maclane:IV.4:def-left-adjoint-left-inverse).

Class Adjunction := { adj {x y} : @Isomorphism Sets {| carrier := @hom C (F x) y |} {| carrier := @hom D x (U y) |}; to_adj_nat_l ...; to_adj_nat_r ...; from_adj_nat_l ...; from_adj_nat_r ... }.

statement_record.book: A Galois connection from P to Q (preorders) is a pair of order-preserving functions L : P -> Q^op, R : Q^op -> P with L p >= q in Q iff p <= R q in P; by Theorem IV.5.1 this is exactly an adjoint pair between the preorders regarded as categories, with L order-reversing as a map P -> Q.
statement_record.intree: Proset (Instance/Proset.v) realizes 'preorder regarded as a (thin) category'; the general Adjunction class (Theory/Adjunction.v) then expresses 'adjoint pair between preorders' when instantiated at Proset categories, with Props_Closed a concrete thin-category adjunction instance; Instance/Poset.v's essay records the identification ('an adjunction between posets is exactly a monotone Galois connection') as prose only.
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only the categorical half of the book's double description is formal (preorders as thin categories + the general adjunction notion); the order-theoretic Galois-connection presentation itself — the pair of monotone maps with the pointwise biconditional, including the antitone Q^op packaging — is never defined, and no formal bridge identifies it with Adjunction at Proset.

gap: No named GaloisConnection definition (neither the monotone L : P -> Q^op / R : Q^op -> P form nor the antitone variant), and no lemma converting the pointwise biconditional L p >= q <-> p <= R q into an Adjunction between the Proset categories (or back); the identification exists only in the background essays of Instance/Poset.v and Theory/Adjunction.v.
